A Whopping 54% Return: How to Profit from Kane County Tax Lien Auction

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

Investing in tax lien certificates through Kane County is a lucrative opportunity, with the potential to earn up to 54% returns in just three years. Held every year on the last Monday of October. This auction allows investors to purchase liens on delinquent properties in Kane County, Illinois, known for its well-connected cities like Geneva and Aurora.

Kane County’s auction follows a bid-down procedure, starting at an interest rate of 9% per six months. Unlike traditional interest, the return on tax liens in Kane County is structured as a penalty. You receive the full 9% penalty, even if the lien is redeemed early, within the first few months. If the property is redeemed later, the penalty escalates to 18% after 12 months. Property owners have between 2.5 and 3 years to redeem their property, which creates significant earning potential for savvy investors.

How Kane County Tax Lien Certificates Work

Tax lien certificates allow investors to pay off a property owner’s delinquent taxes. In return, investors earn a penalty-based return, which is structured as follows:

Initial Interest Rate: Starts at 9% per six months, meaning you can earn up to 18% annually if the lien is redeemed after the first year.

Redemption Period: Property owners have 2.5 to 3 years to redeem their property by paying the back taxes plus penalties.

Failure to Pay: If the property owner does not pay their taxes for the following year, the tax buyer can purchase the subsequent year’s taxes at a 12% interest rate, compounding their returns.

Steps to Participate in Kane County Tax Lien Auction

1. Register for the Tax Lien Auction

  • Registration Period: Opens in September and October.
  • Deposit: A $500 deposit is required to participate, along with a $100 fee for the Tax Sale List.
  • Physical Presence Required: You must attend the auction in person, which takes place at the Kane County Government Center, located at 719 S. Batavia Ave., Geneva, IL.

2. Participate in the Live Auction

  • Auction Date: Held annually on the last Monday of October.
  • Bidding Procedure: Kane County uses a bid-down method, where the interest rate decreases as participants compete to offer the lowest bid.
  • Winning the Bid: The winning bidder earns the right to collect the penalty from the property owner when they pay off their taxes or potentially foreclose on the property if the lien remains unpaid.

3. Post-Auction Procedures

  • Redemption by Property Owners: If the property owner redeems their taxes, you will receive the principal investment plus the interest (penalty) earned.
  • Foreclosure: If the lien is not redeemed within the 2.5 to 3-year period, you can petition for a tax deed, potentially gaining ownership of the property.

FAQs

What is the interest rate for tax lien certificates in Kane County?
The interest rate starts at 9% every six months, calculated as a penalty, not accrued interest.

How long do property owners have to redeem their property?
Property owners have between 2.5 to 3 years to redeem their property by paying back the taxes and penalties.

What happens if the property owner doesn’t pay taxes the following year?
If the owner fails to pay taxes the next year by the third week of September, the previous year’s tax buyer can purchase the new year’s taxes at a 12% annual penalty.

How do I participate in the auction?
Register in September or October, pay the $500 deposit and $100 Tax Sale List fee, and attend the auction in person.
